accepted.s: In Andhra Pradesh, black soils account for approximately what proportion of the land area?
accepted.x: Black soils cover approximately 25 per cent of the land area of Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Use the numerical-value distinction among closely spaced area shares.
accepted.sec: Black soils - districts and crops

accepted.s:
Black soils of Andhra Pradesh are mainly derived from which of the following parent materials?
1. Deccan Trap basalt
2. Crystalline schists
3. Basic gneiss
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The black soils of Andhra Pradesh are derived from Deccan Trap basalt, crystalline schists and basic gneiss.
accepted.tq: Test all listed parent materials together and eliminate partial combinations.
accepted.sec: Black soils - districts and crops

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly describes the chemical nature and texture of black soils in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Fine and clayey, neutral to strongly alkaline
accepted.x: These soils are fine and clayey and generally range from neutral to strongly alkaline.
accepted.tq: Use the paired texture-and-reaction description rather than identifying only one property.
accepted.sec: Black soils - districts and crops

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the nutrient composition of black soils:
1. They are rich in calcium, potash and magnesium.
2. They are poor in nitrogen, phosphorus and humus.
3. They have high water-retention capacity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Black soils are rich in calcium, potash and magnesium, but poor in nitrogen, phosphorus and humus; they also retain water well.
accepted.tq: Separate the positive nutrient traits from the deficiencies and the physical property.
accepted.sec: Black soils - districts and crops

accepted.s: The deep cracks formed in black soil during dry periods are chiefly associated with which agricultural characteristic?
accepted.x: Deep cracks formed on drying loosen and turn the soil, giving black soil its self-ploughing character.
accepted.tq: Link the observed field condition to its recognised agricultural consequence.
accepted.sec: Black soils - districts and crops

accepted.s: Which of the following districts or areas is NOT associated with the distribution of black soils in Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: The Kunderu basin, Adoni, Alur, Nandyal and Kurnool are associated with black soils. Srikakulam and Vizianagaram are not listed among the black-soil areas in this distribution.
accepted.tq: Find the location that does not belong to the stated distribution pattern.
accepted.sec: Black soils - districts and crops

accepted.s: Deep black soils in Andhra Pradesh are particularly associated with which pair of places?
accepted.x: Deep black soils occur particularly at Adoni and Alur.
accepted.tq: Test the specific place pair rather than the broader district distribution.
accepted.sec: Black soils - districts and crops

accepted.s: Which one of the following crops is specifically noted as doing best on black soils in Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: Black gram is specifically identified as doing best on black soils, while mango and cashew suit lateritic soils and coffee suits hill soils.
accepted.tq: Use the crop-soil association and reject crops assigned to other soil groups.
accepted.sec: Black soils - districts and crops

accepted.s: The local names 'Regur' and 'Regadi' refer to which soil of Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: Regur and Regadi are local names for black soil, also called black cotton soil.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between regional names of similar soil categories.
accepted.sec: Black soils - districts and crops

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Black soil — cotton
2. Black soil — jowar
3. Black soil — turmeric
4. Black soil — tobacco
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Cotton, jowar, turmeric and tobacco are among the crops grown on black soils in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Check the complete crop list instead of selecting only the most famous crop.
accepted.sec: Black soils - districts and crops

accepted.s: Deltaic alluvial soils in Andhra Pradesh are primarily formed by the deposition of river-borne silt from which major river systems?
accepted.x: The major deltaic alluvium is laid down by the Godavari and Krishna rivers and is renewed by floods.
accepted.tq: Identify the principal river pair responsible for the formation.
accepted.sec: Deltaic alluvium - formation and delta crops

accepted.s: Why are the deltaic alluvial soils of Andhra Pradesh periodically renewed?
o: Each flood deposits fresh silt over the existing soil.
They are formed by the weathering of crystalline rocks in situ.
They are formed exclusively from volcanic ash.
They are renewed by wind-blown desert sand.
accepted.x: Floods of the major rivers deposit fresh river-borne silt, periodically renewing the deltaic alluvium.
accepted.tq: Connect the geomorphic process with its effect on soil renewal.
accepted.sec: Deltaic alluvium - formation and delta crops

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a characteristic of deltaic alluvial soil in Andhra Pradesh?
o: It is coarse, gravelly and has very low moisture retention.
It is shallow, skeletal and devoid of nutrients.
It is strongly acidic and rich in lateritic iron.
It is porous and loamy and has high moisture retention.
accepted.x: Deltaic alluvial soil is porous and loamy, retains moisture well and is rich in potash and lime.
accepted.tq: Choose the option combining the characteristic physical properties of the soil.
accepted.sec: Deltaic alluvium - formation and delta crops

accepted.s: Approximately what proportion of Andhra Pradesh is covered by its most fertile deltaic alluvial soils?
accepted.x: Deltaic alluvial soils cover approximately 6 per cent of Andhra Pradesh and are regarded as its most fertile soils.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the specific soil-area estimate from the larger black-soil share.
accepted.sec: Deltaic alluvium - formation and delta crops

accepted.s:
Which of the following areas is associated with deltaic alluvial soils in Andhra Pradesh?
1. Konaseema
2. Nellore
3. Anakapalli
4. Guntur
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Konaseema, Nellore, Anakapalli and Guntur are among the areas associated with deltaic alluvial soils.
accepted.tq: Verify each location against the coastal and deltaic distribution.
accepted.sec: Deltaic alluvium - formation and delta crops

accepted.s: The title 'Rice Bowl of Andhra Pradesh' is particularly associated with which zone?
accepted.x: The Godavari zone is known as the Rice Bowl of Andhra Pradesh and is also an aquaculture hub.
accepted.tq: Match the regional title with the correct geographical zone.
accepted.sec: Deltaic alluvium - formation and delta crops

accepted.s: Old alluvium and new alluvium are respectively known as:
accepted.x: Old alluvium is called Bangar, while new alluvium is called Khadar.
accepted.tq: Test the easily reversible pair by requiring the correct sequence.
accepted.sec: Deltaic alluvium - formation and delta crops

accepted.s: Which soil is most suitable for the fertile agricultural tracts of the Krishna-Godavari deltas?
accepted.x: The Krishna-Godavari deltaic tracts are characterised by highly fertile deltaic alluvial soil.
accepted.tq: Use the regional soil-crop setting to identify the most suitable soil.
accepted.sec: Deltaic alluvium - formation and delta crops

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with deltaic alluvial soil?
1. Paddy
2. Sugarcane
3. Vegetables
4. Fruits
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Paddy, sugarcane, vegetables and fruits are among the crops suited to deltaic alluvial soils.
accepted.tq: Test the complete crop group associated with the deltaic environment.
accepted.sec: Deltaic alluvium - formation and delta crops

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding problem soils is correct?
o: Alkalinity increases the availability of all plant nutrients.
Salinity can lower yields and break down soil structure.
Salinity generally improves soil structure and raises yields.
Alkalinity is caused only by excessive organic matter.
accepted.x: Salinity lowers crop yields and may break down soil structure. Alkalinity reduces nutrient availability and may be associated with limestone, basalt or alkaline irrigation water.
accepted.tq: Reject the reversed effect and identify the precise soil-problem consequence.
accepted.sec: Problem soils - saline, alkaline, acidic, waterlogged

accepted.s: Which soil type is associated with acidic conditions, while black soil generally shows a neutral to strongly alkaline tendency?
accepted.x: Laterite soils are associated with acidic conditions, whereas black soils are generally neutral to strongly alkaline.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the acidic and alkaline soil associations.
accepted.sec: Problem soils - saline, alkaline, acidic, waterlogged

accepted.s: A farmer observes reduced nutrient availability in a field irrigated with alkaline water. Which soil problem best explains the condition?
accepted.x: Alkalinity, which may result from alkaline irrigation water, reduces the availability of nutrients to plants.
accepted.tq: Apply the cause-effect relationship to a practical agricultural situation.
accepted.sec: Problem soils - saline, alkaline, acidic, waterlogged

accepted.s: The Soil Health Card Scheme was launched in which year?
accepted.x: The Soil Health Card Scheme was launched in 2015.
accepted.tq: Test the scheme year against nearby policy years.
accepted.sec: Soil Health Card and soil testing

accepted.s:
Which of the following functions is associated with Soil Health Cards?
1. Analysis of soil samples
2. Village-wise nutrient mapping
3. Assessment of soil nutrient status for farm management
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Soil Health Cards provide soil-sample analysis and village-wise nutrient mapping, helping farmers understand soil nutrient status.
accepted.tq: Combine the scheme's diagnostic and mapping functions in a coded statement question.
accepted.sec: Soil Health Card and soil testing

accepted.s: The Soil Health and Fertility component has been operated under which programme since 2022-23?
accepted.x: Since 2022-23, Soil Health and Fertility has been operated under the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY).
accepted.tq: Use the implementing-programme trap by distinguishing related agricultural initiatives.
accepted.sec: Soil Health Card and soil testing

accepted.s: During 2025-26, soil sampling in Andhra Pradesh was carried out through how many Rythu Seva Kendras?
accepted.x: Sampling was carried out through 10,778 Rythu Seva Kendras across all 26 districts of Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the institutional count from the sample and district figures.
accepted.sec: Soil Health Card and soil testing

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the soil-testing figures for Andhra Pradesh in 2025-26?
o: 5.523 lakh samples collected and 6.0 lakh tested and uploaded
26 lakh samples collected and 6.0 lakh tested and uploaded
10.778 lakh samples collected and 5.0 lakh tested and uploaded
6.0 lakh samples collected and 5.523 lakh tested and uploaded
accepted.x: In 2025-26, 6.0 lakh samples were collected, of which 5.523 lakh were tested and uploaded.
accepted.tq: Keep the collection and testing figures in their correct order.
accepted.sec: Soil Health Card and soil testing

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the School Soil Health Programme in Andhra Pradesh during 2025-26?
o: It covered 10 Kendriya Vidyalayas and 50 State schools.
It covered 50 Kendriya Vidyalayas and 10 State schools.
It covered 50 State schools and 50 Kendriya Vidyalayas only.
It covered all 26 districts but no schools.
accepted.x: The programme operated in 50 Kendriya Vidyalayas and 10 State schools.
accepted.tq: Separate the two school categories and their respective counts.
accepted.sec: Soil Health Card and soil testing

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes the characteristic condition of Rayalaseema's red soils?
o: Permanently waterlogged and rich in humus
Shallow, with low moisture retention and low organic matter
Deep, highly moist and rich in organic matter
accepted.x: Rayalaseema's red soils are shallow and have low moisture-retention capacity and low organic matter.
accepted.tq: Select the combined physical and fertility profile of the regional soil.
accepted.sec: Soil erosion and land degradation in Rayalaseema

accepted.s: Heavily eroded tracts of Rayalaseema may develop skeletal soils that are characterised by:
o: High nutrient value and deep profiles
High water retention and abundant humus
accepted.x: Severe erosion in Rayalaseema can leave skeletal soils with no nutritive value.
accepted.tq: Infer the soil-quality outcome from the stated erosion process.
accepted.sec: Soil erosion and land degradation in Rayalaseema

accepted.s: Which type of soil generally retains more soil organic carbon than sandy soil and soil on steep slopes?
accepted.x: Clay soils hold more soil organic carbon, whereas sandy soils and steep slopes lose it through leaching and erosion.
accepted.tq: Use the relative retention comparison rather than the erosion causes alone.
accepted.sec: Soil erosion and land degradation in Rayalaseema

accepted.s:
Which area-damage pair is correctly matched?
1. Anantapur and Sri Sathya Sai — drought-induced degradation, desertification and wind erosion
2. Uppada — coastal erosion from sea-level rise and waves
3. Delta regions — salinity and waterlogging
4. ASR and Parvathipuram Manyam — topsoil loss through Podu cultivation
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four area-problem pairs are correctly matched: drought and wind erosion in Anantapur and Sri Sathya Sai, coastal erosion at Uppada, salinity and waterlogging in deltas, and topsoil loss through Podu cultivation in ASR and Parvathipuram Manyam.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure location-problem pairs and verify the complete table.
accepted.sec: Soil erosion and land degradation in Rayalaseema

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a cause of soil degradation in the Andhra Pradesh regions under consideration?
o: Periodic deposition of fresh deltaic silt
accepted.x: Overgrazing, deforestation and erratic rainfall contribute to degradation. Periodic deposition of fresh deltaic silt is a soil-renewal process, not a stated cause of degradation.
accepted.tq: Find the process with a beneficial rather than degrading effect.
accepted.sec: Soil erosion and land degradation in Rayalaseema

accepted.s: Heavy chemical use is specifically associated with soil degradation in which crop belts of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Guntur chilli and Krishna paddy belts
Rayalaseema mango and groundnut belts only
Godavari rice and aquaculture belts only
accepted.x: Heavy chemical use is identified as a degradation cause in the Guntur chilli and Krishna paddy belts.
accepted.tq: Match the degrading practice with the correct crop belts.
accepted.sec: Soil erosion and land degradation in Rayalaseema

accepted.s: Which intervention is intended to restore soil organic carbon through natural farming?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh Community-Managed Natural Farming (APCNF) is intended to restore soil organic carbon.
accepted.tq: Identify the programme from its stated ecological function.
accepted.sec: Soil erosion and land degradation in Rayalaseema

accepted.s: Rainfed Area Development in Andhra Pradesh covers which set of districts?
o: Nine rainfed districts: eight Rayalaseema districts and Prakasam
Only the three Godavari delta districts
accepted.x: The programme covers nine rainfed districts, comprising the eight Rayalaseema districts and Prakasam.
accepted.tq: Use the composition of the district group to reject broader or narrower claims.
accepted.sec: Soil erosion and land degradation in Rayalaseema

accepted.s: Under Rainfed Area Development, the assistance specified per farm family is:
accepted.x: The specified assistance is ₹30,000 per farm family.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact assistance amount by place value.
accepted.sec: Soil erosion and land degradation in Rayalaseema

accepted.s:
Which of the following crop-soil pairs is correctly matched?
1. Paddy — deltaic alluvial soil
2. Cotton — black soil
3. Groundnut — red soil
4. Mango — laterite soil
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Paddy suits deltaic alluvium, cotton suits black soil, groundnut suits red soil and mango suits laterite soil.
accepted.tq: Build the answer from familiar crop-soil associations across the table.
accepted.sec: Soil-crop suitability in AP

accepted.s: Which crop group is most appropriately associated with red soils in Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: Groundnut, castor and millets are associated with red soils.
accepted.tq: Separate the red-soil crop group from black- and deltaic-soil crops.
accepted.sec: Soil-crop suitability in AP

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding pulses and soil suitability is correct?
o: All pulses are restricted to deltaic alluvial soil.
Red, green and horse gram suit red soil, while black gram does best on black soil.
Black gram is exclusively a laterite-soil crop.
Pulses are best suited only to hill skeletal soils.
accepted.x: Red gram, green gram and horse gram are associated with red soil, while black gram does best on black soil.
accepted.tq: Discriminate within the pulse group instead of treating all pulses identically.
accepted.sec: Soil-crop suitability in AP

accepted.s: Mango and cashew are most appropriately associated with which soil type in Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: Mango and cashew are identified as crops suited to laterite soils.
accepted.tq: Match the horticultural crops with their specific soil group.
accepted.sec: Soil-crop suitability in AP

accepted.s: Coffee, tea and horticulture in the ASR region are associated with which soil category?
accepted.x: Coffee, tea and horticulture are associated with hill, or skeletal, soils in the ASR region.
accepted.tq: Use the regional crop association to identify the hill-soil category.
accepted.sec: Soil-crop suitability in AP
